# dsh-model-pool
**English** · 简体中文
A DeepSeek Harness plugin that turns **every registered provider into one model pool**.

You pick a model *once* — the pool decides which concrete provider serves each call,
according to a

strategy you choose. If a provider is down, the pool skips it, fails over
to the next candidate, and
marks it unavailable in the UI until it recovers.
[代码示例省略，未执行]
## Why

Providers overlap. `deepseek-v4-pro` may be served by the first-party account *and* by a
third-party

route; `deepseek-v4.1-flash` may exist on several. Today you must pick one
route per session and re

member which one is healthy. This plugin makes the *model* the
unit of choice and the *provider* an
implementation detail.
## Install

**Requirements:** DeepSeek Harness Desktop or CLI, Node.js **>= 20**. No build step and no
runtime d

ependencies — the Host half is plain ESM, the browser half is a hand-written
`window.__ModuleLoader_

_` module that only `require('react')`s. The two peer dependencies
(`@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm`, `@deepse

ek-ai/schemastery`) are provided by the Host, so nothing
has to be installed alongside the plugin.
### DSH Desktop

Open the **plugin manager**, search the registry for `dsh-model-pool`, and install it.
Restart DSH D

manager**, search the registry for `dsh-model-pool`, and install it.
Restart DSH Desktop afterwards.
### CLI profiles
[代码示例省略，未执行]

`dsh plugin` delegates to pnpm inside the profile directory and selects the bundle in
`dsh.profile.b
undles`. Restart the profile afterwards.
### Local checkout
[代码示例省略，未执行]

That is the development install: pnpm links the checkout instead of downloading it, so the
next rest
art picks up your edits.
### Verify

- **Settings → Model Pool** exists, and lists every pooled model with its provider count,
thinking d

epths and per-route state badges.
- The composer model picker contains a **Model Pool** entry; pick

one of its models and each
call is routed through the pool.

Both halves ship in the same package: `dsh.bundle.patch` is the Host half (`index.js` +
`lib/`) and

`dsh.client` is the browser half (`client.js`). Nothing is built at install
time.
The full guide, including troubleshooting, is in `docs/installation.md`.
## Use

1. Open **Settings → Model Pool**. It lists every pooled model, how many providers serve
it, its thi

nking depths, and a per-route state badge.
2. Choose a **strategy** (below) and the behaviour switch

es. Optionally give the peak and
the idle period their own provider ranking in the **峰谷时段（peak / idl

e）** card, which
also shows the live period, when it next flips, and the statutory holiday calendar

that
the plugin keeps in sync by itself — there is nothing to fill in by hand.
3. In the composer mo

del picker, pick a **Model Pool** model and a thinking depth.
4. Each call is routed; failures cool
a route down and fail over to the next candidate.
## Strategies
| Strategy | What it does | When to use |
| `priority` | Try providers in the configured priority order. | A clear first choice (e.g. first-pa

rty) with a backup. |
| `round-robin` | Rotate the starting provider on every call. | Spread load ev

enly across equivalent routes. |
| `weighted-random` | Draw at random, honouring each provider's wei

ght. | Keep traffic mostly on a preferred route without hard pinning. |
| `least-used` | Prefer the

provider that has served the fewest calls. | Balance without a strict rotation. |
| `fastest` | Pref
er the lowest recent time-to-first-chunk. | Latency-sensitive work; adapts as providers slow down. |
| `cheapest` | Prefer the lowest declared cost hint. | Cost-sensitive bulk work. |

`priority`, `least-used`, `fastest` and `cheapest` are stable: equal keys keep the
priority order, s

o routing never becomes unpredictable. `fastest` learns from real calls
(an EWMA of time-to-first-ch
unk), so the first call on each route is a probe.
### Keeping one conversation on one route
`sticky` (on by default) pins a conversation to the route that served its first call:
| | Without sticky | With sticky |

| `round-robin`, four turns in one chat | `A B C A` | `A A A A` |
| A second chat | continues the ro
tation | picks its own route, then stays |

The point is the provider's prompt cache: re-deciding every turn throws away the cached
[该节后续省略]
## How it works

The Host's `llm` service exposes provider routes; the composer picker and Settings read
them through
`listProviders()` / `listModels()` / `resolveModelInfo()`. This plugin:

1. Registers **one extra virtual route** (`model-pool`) whose models are the union of
every other pr

ovider's models, grouped by normalized model name. That is what makes
the pool appear in the ordinar

y picker, thinking-depth menu included. Each pooled model
advertises the union of its candidates' in

put modalities (see
Images and other input), so a pooled model accepts a
screenshot when *any* of it

s providers can read one.
2. Listens on the **`llm/stream` waterfall**. A request naming the pool ro

ute is
intercepted *before* dispatch and re-issued against a concrete provider chosen by the
strateg

y. A request that carries an image only considers the candidates that accept one,
so the advertised

capability is honoured instead of merely declared. The runtime then
performs exactly one correct pro

jection of files, images and tool history for the real
target.
3. Keeps a **health registry** per co

ncrete route, which feeds both the failover gate and
the Settings badges.

The adapter's own `stream()` never runs; it exists only to claim the route so the catalog
surfaces i

t. If it is ever reached, it fails with a clear message instead of silently
returning nothing.

See `docs/CONTRACT.md` for the verified API evidence and the full
module contract.
